visuals.title: Where myeloma does damage
visuals.text: Plasma cells in the marrow attack bone, blood counts and the kidneys; high calcium causes confusion.

visuals.title: From suspicion to diagnosis
nodes: Free light chains + urine Bence Jones
Bone marrow biopsy: >10% clonal plasma cells

glossary.Malignancy: A cancer: cells growing uncontrollably and able to invade or spread.
glossary.Post-germinal centre B cells: B cells that have matured in a lymph node germinal centre, the stage from which plasma cells arise.
glossary.Germinal centre: Area within lymph nodes where B cells multiply and refine their antibodies.
glossary.Monoclonal: Arising from one single clone of cells, so all the antibody made is identical.
glossary.Immunoglobulin: Another word for antibody, made by plasma cells.
glossary.Marrow failure: When the bone marrow cannot make enough red cells, white cells or platelets.
glossary.Hypercalcaemia: A raised blood calcium level, causing confusion, constipation, thirst and polyuria.
glossary.Urea: A waste product of protein breakdown cleared by the kidneys; rises in renal impairment.
glossary.Creatinine: A muscle waste product cleared by the kidneys; a raised level shows reduced kidney function.
glossary.Normochromic: Red cells with a normal amount of haemoglobin, so normal colour on the film.
glossary.Pallor: Unusual paleness of the skin or conjunctivae, often from anaemia.
glossary.Monoclonal band: A single sharp spike on protein electrophoresis showing one clone's antibody.
glossary.Hypercalcaemic crisis: Dangerously high calcium causing confusion, vomiting, dehydration and arrhythmia; needs urgent treatment.
glossary.Migratory thrombophlebitis: Recurrent clots in superficial veins at different sites, a sign of pancreatic and other cancers.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test available for making a diagnosis.
glossary.Myeloma screen: Set of tests for myeloma: serum protein electrophoresis, serum free light chains and urine Bence Jones protein.
glossary.Aspirate: Fluid or cells sucked out through a needle for examination.
glossary.Clonal: Descended from one abnormal cell, so all cells are identical.
glossary.Punched-out lesions: Sharp-edged holes in bone on X-ray where bone has been destroyed.
glossary.Blood film: A thin smear of blood on a slide examined under the microscope.
glossary.Chemotherapy: Drugs that kill rapidly dividing cancer cells.
glossary.Regimen: A planned schedule of drugs, doses and timing.
glossary.Prednisolone: An oral corticosteroid used here as part of anti-myeloma treatment.
glossary.Stem cell transplantation: Infusion of blood-forming stem cells to rebuild the marrow after high-dose chemotherapy.
glossary.Autologous: Using the patient's own cells, collected before treatment and returned afterwards.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging; the scan of choice for suspected spinal cord compression.
glossary.AKI: Acute kidney injury: a rapid fall in kidney function over hours to days.
glossary.Sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.Immunosuppression: Reduced ability of the immune system to fight infection.
glossary.Naproxen: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug; avoided in myeloma because it can harm the kidneys.
glossary.Ibuprofen: A common non-steroidal anti-inflammatory painkiller; avoided in myeloma due to renal risk.
glossary.Terminally differentiated: Fully mature cells that have reached their final specialised form.
glossary.Cytokines: Small signalling proteins that cells release to influence other cells.
glossary.Bone resorption: Breakdown of bone by osteoclasts, releasing calcium into the blood.
glossary.Renal tubules: The small tubes in the kidney that modify filtered fluid into urine.
glossary.Haematopoiesis: Production of new blood cells in the bone marrow.
glossary.Premalignant: An abnormal state that is not yet cancer but can turn into it.
glossary.Dyscrasia: An abnormal state of blood cells; plasma cell dyscrasias include MGUS and myeloma.
glossary.Lytic: Bone-destroying; lytic lesions are areas where bone has been eaten away.
